title: Stop creating an HttpClient per call
summary: A new HttpClient per call exhausts sockets. Move to a typed client with AddHttpClient, then give the one a singleton captures a PooledConnectionLifetime so it follows DNS changes.

turns.user: load test spews SocketException. netstat shows a crazy amount of TIME_WAIT

assistant.body: TL;DR: WeatherClient builds and throws away an HttpClient on every call. Dispose closes the connection, but the socket stays in TIME_WAIT for a while, so under load the ports run out first. WeatherClient should take its HttpClient from DI as a typed client registered with AddHttpClient. IHttpClientFactory manages handler lifetimes, so ForecastCache can stay exactly as it is.

turns.user: sockets are fine now. but after they switched DNS we kept hitting the old IP until a restart

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. ForecastCache is a singleton, so it keeps the WeatherClient it got in its constructor, and the HttpClient inside it, until the process exits. The factory only rotates handlers for clients it creates from now on, and the captured one keeps its old connections. The shape Microsoft recommends here is to give the connections themselves a lifetime with PooledConnectionLifetime on SocketsHttpHandler, and switch off the factory rotation.

turns.user: their failover flips in 30s apparently. 2 minutes is too long

assistant.body: Only the connection lifetime changes. More reconnects, but the client follows a failover within 30 seconds.
